strategies.name: premarket_range_liquidity_sweep_reversal
strategies.entry_summary: At same pre-market high/low, watch for liquidity sweep: brief fakeout past the level that fails and reclaims; enter OPPOSITE the failed break on reclaim (sweep below low -> long).
strategies.exit_summary: Stop opposite side of entry candle; target >=1x, ideally 1.5-2x; trail to breakeven then profit, scale out, let run.

range_definition.action: after 3:00 a.m. Eastern time all the way up into New York market open, which is going to be 9:30 a.m. EST, you want to find the highest point of price action, and you want to find the lowest point of price action
range_definition.supporting_quote: mark the highest high of that price action and the lowest low of that price action

entry_sequence.action: we want to look for liquidity sweeps at those pre-market highs or those pre-market lows
A liquidity sweep is going to be a brief fake out below or above the level

you have your London low, price tries to break below it, reclaims it right away, or it does break below it a little bit, but comes back up and reclaims the overall level. That's going to be a liquidity sweep
entry_sequence.note_short_side: we have our highest point of price action from the London high. Price tries to break above it. Maybe it closes above the range a little bit, maybe it wicks above it, but overall it fails that level and it comes back down and closes below

entry_sequence.action: we enter on the confirmation after the retest of the level, after the breakout of the level, or after the liquidity sweep of the level
Price breaks below but reclaims the level with a lot of volume. You are going to look to get long
entry_sequence.rationale: you have both sides of the market getting stopped out. Anyone who is long over here getting stopped out as price breaks below. Anyone who's shorting over here is getting stopped out as we reclaim the area which usually sets up for a pretty powerful and aggressive move the opposite way

confluences.description: reclaims the level with a lot of volume

if you use orderflow such as bookmap, there is something called a stops indicator that I really love to use. And you usually can identify these liquidity suites with high probability by simply just looking at the stops indicator

stop.description: The stop is always going to go on the opposite side of the entry candle
stop.supporting_quote: Your stop loss has to be below your entry candle

targets.description: bare minimum of 1x of my original risk
ideally what I'm looking for is a 1.5x to a 2x my original risk

trade_management.description: as the trade continues to move in my favor, I'm going to be looking to trail my stop-loss up at least to break even, ideally in profits, and to just let that sucker run. and I'll continue to scale out as it moves in my favor, continue to move my stop loss up
trade_management.supporting_quote: move your stop-loss up and let that thing run until you are either stopped out or satisfied with your profits

timeframe.primary: I trade the five-minute time frame

strategies.session: this setup starts at 3:00 a.m. Eastern time ... all the way up into New York market open, which is going to be 9:30 a.m. EST

instrument_classification.instruments_named: popular future instruments like the S&P 500 futures, the NASDAQ futures, or even the Dow futures
instrument_classification.notes: Index-futures price-action/level strategy on the 5-minute timeframe. No options Greeks/strikes; no instrument-specific mechanic that would disqualify.
